# VibeLoom

> Contract-driven agentic engineering — an open-source Skill plus a deterministic Python engine that gives AI coding agents a multi-tier contract that humans author and agents are compiled against, with drift detection, approval gates, and reconciliation across the lifecycle.

VibeLoom is the v0.3 reference implementation of **codæ** — contract-driven agentic engineering. codæ is the next step beyond per-feature spec-driven development (GitHub Spec Kit, AWS Kiro, BMAD): instead of treating specifications as one-off planning documents that decay after the first generation pass, codæ maintains a multi-tier, mutually-derived, graph-tied contract that doubles as the eval surface for every subsequent change. The contract is more formal than prose, less formal than first-order logic — structured markdown with stable IDs and explicit derivation links, plus a deterministic engine that detects drift the moment it appears.

The methodology and engine are open source under MIT license. v0.3 ships as a Skill for Claude Code and Codex plus a deterministic Python 3.10+ engine with zero runtime dependencies.

## Concepts

- **Contract stack** — four contract tiers plus context: **intent-specs → product-specs ⇄ ux-specs → system-specs → context → code**. Each tier derives from the approved tier above; `product-specs` and `ux-specs` are peer co-informing tiers. Upstream items are the eval basis for downstream work.
- **Three working layers** — **Contract** (governed truth; only approved items drive downstream generation), **Context** (active generation guidance derived from approved contract), **Code** (executable result; synchronized and validated, not approved). Traces run alongside as durable append-only provenance.
- **Contract Graph** — DAG of IDed semantic items (entities) connected by typed `derives_from` edges. Built by the engine from frontmatter declarations; persisted to `.vibeloom/cache/contract-graph.json` (regenerable). Powers derivation order, affected-set computation, drift detection, scoped subagent dispatch, traceability.
- **Five modes** — `vibe` (compact, solo, one gate, no graph or code-sync), `pm` (product-led), `dev` (tech-led), `ux` (design-led with mockups as primary evidence), `expert` (all gates explicit). Vibe → full upgrade is one-way and produces an explicit migration trace.
- **Eight operations** — `init`, `import`, `generate`, `eval`, `review`, `reconcile`, `approve`, `status`. Orthogonal — none does another's job. Plus `$vibeloom` shorthand that triages by current state.
- **Verification ladder** — three tiers: **decidable** (structural eval — boolean checks, no LLM), **mechanical** (project-defined runners — typecheck, lint, tests, contract conformance), **heuristic** (semantic eval — agent-judged). The trajectory: promote checks upward as the engine matures.
- **Six trace families** — `approval`, `generation`, `eval`, `code-sync`, `decision`, `import` (plus `id-registry`). Append-only JSONL streams in `.vibeloom/traces/`. Never silently regenerated. Approval traces carry per-item content fingerprints — the substrate for drift detection.
- **Drift forms** — *structural* (upstream item changed since downstream synchronized), *lifecycle* (approved file edited outside the flow), *semantic* (downstream meaning shifted even when structure passes). Distinct from the multi-agent agent-drift triad (semantic/coordination/behavioral).
- **Status categories** — `current`, `stale`, `uncovered`, `dangling`, `drifted`, `obsolete`. `uncovered` is distinct from `stale` — newly approved upstream creates downstream obligations that no item can yet depend on.
- **Two-layer architecture** — the **Skill** (semantic judgment, mode selection, approval gates, subagent orchestration) plus the deterministic **engine** (parsing, schema validation, Contract Graph construction, structural eval, drift detection, dispatch planning). They cooperate through `.vibeloom/` — regenerable cache plus durable append-only traces. The engine never decides product meaning.

## Empirical anchors

The codæ argument is grounded in 28 contemporary citations (2025–2026) plus four foundational works (Meyer's Design by Contract, Brooks's *No Silver Bullet*, Evans's *Domain-Driven Design*, Fowler & Parsons's *Domain-Specific Languages*). Load-bearing 2026 anchors include:

- **Anthropic randomized controlled trial** on coding-skill formation (Feb 2026): 17% lower mastery with AI assistance; the layer of delegation determines whether skill is preserved (65%+ for conceptual inquiry vs <40% for delegated code generation).
- **Margaret-Anne Storey** (Canada Research Chair, March 2026): proposes the Triple Debt Model — technical debt + cognitive debt + *intent debt* (the absence of externalized rationale that developers and AI agents need to work safely with code).
- **Martin Fowler** (Thoughtworks Chief Scientist, February 2026): ratifies Storey's diagnosis at the Future of Software Development Retreat — "cognitive cruft is ignorance, both of the code and the domain the code is supporting."
- **MIT Media Lab** (Kos'myna et al.): EEG study introducing the term *cognitive debt* — LLM users showed weakest brain connectivity and underperformed across four sessions.
- **Anthropic** *How AI is Transforming Work* (Q1 2026): names the *paradox of supervision* — effectively using Claude requires the very coding skills AI overuse erodes.
- **SlopCodeBench** (Mar 2026): 80%/89.8% of agent trajectories show rising erosion/verbosity on long-horizon iterative coding tasks.
- **CMU Cursor study** (MSR 2026): short-term velocity gain dissipates after 2 months, leaving +30% warnings and +41% complexity.
- **Lars Faye** *Agentic Coding is a Trap* (Apr 2026, 391 HN points): the viral critique of fragile spec-driven scaffolding. codæ shares the diagnosis and builds the scaffolding that doesn't fail it.

## How VibeLoom compares to spec-driven development tools

- **GitHub Spec Kit** — open-source spec-driven workflow with constitution + per-feature specify/plan/tasks. Strong durable layer at the constitution; per-feature artifacts decay post-merge. Source: https://github.com/github/spec-kit
- **AWS Kiro** — IDE-bound feature spec workflow (requirements → design → tasks) plus steering files and hooks. Strong feature documentation; per-feature specs go static post-creation. Source: https://kiro.dev/docs/specs/feature-specs/
- **BMAD** — workflow-with-personas approach (PM, Architect, Dev, QA) for per-feature ceremony. Strong role separation; no whole-system contract.
- **Tessl** — pivoted from per-file `spec-as-source` toward per-skill context management. Same direction as VibeLoom, smaller scope.
- **VibeLoom** — whole-system contract for one codebase, graph-connected from intent down to component, with explicit drift detection and reconciliation across every change.

## Honest limitations

- v0.3 — public field evidence is still early. Adoption should begin in `vibe` mode or via brownfield `import` before a team commits to full governance.
- DDD vocabulary in full modes (bounded contexts, ubiquitous language, aggregates) narrows the addressable market.
- Contracts decay too if nobody maintains them. The Contract Graph detects drift but does not prevent cultural neglect.
- The dark-factory trajectory is a 2-3 year bet, not a v0.3 promise. Today's agents are not yet trustworthy enough to leave alone with the code.
